Today we remember the prophet Malachi, who promised that the sun of righteousness would rise with healing in its wings (Malachi 4:2), and St Kuriakose Elias Chavara, who lived the Beatitudes among the poor of Kerala, building schools and homes of prayer.
On Wednesday we celebrate Denho, when that Sun rises at the Jordan. Let us choose one Beatitude to live this week, and prepare our hearts to see God. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: happy are the kind, the gentle and the peacemakers! Choose one this week. Will you be a peacemaker at home?

homily: Dear friends, St Paul tells the Ephesians that the risen Christ gave gifts to his Church: apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors and teachers, to equip the saints for the work of ministry, for building up the body of Christ (Ephesians 4:11–12). Every gift is for others.
The goal is maturity: speaking the truth in love, we must grow up in every way into him who is the head, into Christ (Ephesians 4:15). Not truth without love, and not love without truth.

In the Gospel Jesus says: do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear. Consider the ravens; consider the lilies. They neither toil nor spin, yet even Solomon in all his glory was not clothed like one of these (Luke 12:22, 27).

Today we remember the erection of our Eparchy of St Mary, Queen of Peace, in the USA and Canada. Many of our families live far from home under heavy pressure. Jesus says to them and to us: your Father knows what you need.
Tonight is the eve of Denho. Tomorrow the Father will speak at the Jordan: this is my beloved Son. Let us lay down our worries tonight and come tomorrow as children who trust their Father. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: look at the flowers! God makes them so beautiful. If God takes care of flowers, he will surely take care of you. Don't be afraid!

homily: Dear friends, on the day after Denho the Syriac Churches praise John the Baptist, who baptised the Lord in the Jordan. Jesus himself speaks his praise.

He asks the crowds: what did you go out into the wilderness to look at? A reed shaken by the wind? (Luke 7:24). No. John was not shaken by public opinion or by Herod's power. Someone dressed in soft robes? No. John lived in poverty.
A prophet? Yes, says Jesus, and more than a prophet. He is the messenger sent ahead to prepare the way. Among those born of women no one is greater than John (Luke 7:28).

Then a surprise: yet the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he. John stood at the door; by Baptism we have entered. This is not about our merit but about grace. Paul calls himself a servant of the gospel according to the gift of God's grace (Ephesians 3:7).
Let us honour John by being firm in faith, simple in life, and grateful for the Kingdom we have received. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said John the Baptist was very great and strong, like a tree in a storm. Let us be strong for Jesus too!

homily: Dear friends, in the days after Denho the Syriac Churches honour Mar Stephanos, the first martyr. At the Jordan the Baptist saw the heavens open. At his death Stephen sees the same: I see the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God (Acts 7:56).
Jesus is standing, as if rising to welcome his witness. The council covers their ears and rushes at him. They stone him. A young man named Saul guards their coats.

And Stephen prays as Jesus prayed on the Cross: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit. Then he kneels and cries out: Lord, do not hold this sin against them (Acts 7:59–60). He dies forgiving. Later, that young Saul becomes Paul the Apostle. The martyr's prayer bore fruit.

Jesus had foretold it: I send you prophets, sages, and scribes, some of whom you will kill (Matthew 23:34). Stephen began as a deacon serving tables and ended with the crown of martyrdom. Service and witness are one road.
Today is the name day of Bishop Philipos Mar Stephanos; we pray for him. Let us ask for Stephen's faith to see heaven, his love to forgive, and his humility to serve. Amen.
kids: Children, Stephen loved Jesus very much. Even when people hurt him, he prayed for them. Let us pray for anyone who has hurt us.

homily: Dear friends, the Pharisees and scribes see Jesus' disciples eating with unwashed hands, against the tradition of the elders. They complain. Jesus answers with Isaiah: this people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me (Mark 7:6).

Jesus is not against tradition. Our Church lives by Holy Tradition, received from the Apostles. He is against human customs that replace God's commandment: you abandon the commandment of God and hold to human tradition (Mark 7:8).
St Paul asks: if some were unfaithful, will their faithlessness nullify the faithfulness of God? By no means! Let God be proved true (Romans 3:3–4). God's faithfulness is stronger than our failures.

A few days ago we celebrated Denho, the Baptism of the Lord. In our Baptism God washed not our hands but our hearts. Let us check our customs and devotions: do they come from the heart? Do they lead us to love God and neighbour? Then they are holy. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said God cares most about a clean heart. Washing hands is good, but a kind and loving heart is even better!

intro: Theme: “Begin the year in the name of Jesus.”
On the eighth day the Child received the name the angel had given: Jesus, “God saves”. We begin the new year not with luck or fear but with a name: the name above every name.

points.h: The name that reveals who he is
sub: At the burning bush God revealed his name to Moses: a name to be remembered for all generations.
In Jesus that name becomes a person: “God saves”.
Mary and Joseph obey the angel: they give the name God chose.
q: This is my name forever, and this my title for all generations.
After eight days had passed, it was time to circumcise the child; and he was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
points.apply: Say the name of Jesus with reverence; never use it carelessly.

points.h: There is no other saving name
sub: The prophets promised: whoever calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.
Peter proclaimed: there is no other name under heaven by which we must be saved.
In every need of the coming year, call on this name with faith.
q: Then everyone who calls on the name of the LORD shall be saved.
There is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among mortals by which we must be saved.
points.apply: Make the short prayer “Jesus, I trust in you” your companion this year.

points.h: A new year, a new self
sub: The priests of Israel blessed the people by placing God's name upon them.
Mary and Joseph presented the Child to the Lord; we present this new year to him.
St Paul tells us to put off the old self and put on the new, created in righteousness and holiness.
q: The LORD bless you and keep you; the LORD make his face to shine upon you, and be gracious to you; the LORD lift up his countenance upon you, and give you peace.
Clothe yourselves with the new self, created according to the likeness of God in true righteousness and holiness.
points.apply: Write one resolution for the year that will make you more like Christ, and offer it at the altar today.

concl: Whatever this year brings, it is placed under the name of Jesus.
Let us begin it blessed, cleansed and renewed, calling on the name that saves.
2027-01-01.resolve: Bless your family with the words of Numbers 6:24–26 at the start of each month this year.

intro: Theme: “Behold the Lamb of God.”
John the Baptist points away from himself to Jesus: “Here is the Lamb of God.” He also tells ordinary people how to prepare for him: by concrete repentance in daily life.

sub: Isaiah saw a silent Servant led like a lamb to the slaughter.
John recognises Jesus as the Lamb who takes away the sin of the world.
The Church calls Christ the Lamb in her liturgy; in the Holy Qurbono we receive the Lamb who was sacrificed for us.
q: Like a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and like a sheep that before its shearers is silent, so he did not open his mouth.
Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!
points.apply: Look at the Holy Mysteries at the elevation and say in your heart: “Lamb of God, have mercy on me.”

sub: The crowds ask: “What then should we do?”
John's answers are practical: share your coat and food; collect only what is just; do not threaten or accuse falsely.
Isaiah too: cease to do evil, learn to do good, defend the orphan and the widow.
q: Cease to do evil, learn to do good; seek justice, rescue the oppressed, defend the orphan, plead for the widow.
And the crowds asked him, “What then should we do?” In reply he said to them, “Whoever has two coats must share with anyone who has none; and whoever has food must do likewise.”
points.apply: Give away one good garment or one day's food to someone in need this week.

sub: The boy Samuel grew in favour with God and people while serving in the Temple.
John saw the Spirit descend and testified: “This is the Son of God.”
Every Christian is called to grow in faith and to bear witness, not to himself, but to Christ.
q: Now the boy Samuel continued to grow both in stature and in favor with the LORD and with the people.
And I myself have seen and have testified that this is the Son of God.
points.apply: Speak of Jesus simply to one person this week: what he means to you.

concl: John's whole life is a finger pointing to Christ.
Let our lives too say to others: “Behold the Lamb of God.”
2027-01-03.resolve: Pray each night this week: “Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world, have mercy on us.”

intro: Theme: “The heavens opened: the Son, the Spirit, the Father, and our Baptism.”
Denho means “dawning” or “manifestation”. At the Jordan Jesus is revealed as the beloved Son, the Spirit rests on him, and the Father speaks. Today we also remember our own Baptism.

points.h: The sinless One enters our waters
sub: John protests: “I need to be baptized by you.”
Jesus answers: “Let it be so now; it is proper for us to fulfil all righteousness”: he stands with sinners.
The Fathers say: he did not need the waters to make him holy; he made the waters holy for us.
q: I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be clean from all your uncleannesses, and from all your idols I will cleanse you.
But Jesus answered him, “Let it be so now; for it is proper for us in this way to fulfill all righteousness.” Then he consented.
points.apply: Thank God for the humility of Christ, who stands in line with sinners.

sub: The heavens are torn apart: God's distance is overcome.
The Spirit descends like a dove; the Father's voice declares the beloved Son.
Isaiah's servant, filled with the Spirit, is revealed: Jesus is the Christ, the Anointed.
q: Here is my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my spirit upon him; he will bring forth justice to the nations.

And just as he was coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens torn apart and the Spirit descending like a dove on him. And a voice came from heaven, “You are my Son, the Beloved; with you I am well pleased.”
points.apply: Make the sign of the Cross today slowly, thinking of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

points.h: Our Baptism: drawing water from the wells of salvation
sub: Isaiah promised joy from the wells of salvation.
In Baptism the same Spirit came upon us; in Chrismation we were sealed with holy Myron.
St Paul's disciples at Ephesus received the Spirit when hands were laid on them.
q: With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation.
He saved us, not because of any works of righteousness that we had done, but according to his mercy, through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit.
points.apply: Find out the date of your Baptism and celebrate it every year.

concl: At the Jordan heaven opened; at our Baptism heaven opened for us.
Let us live as beloved children of the Father, filled with the Spirit, following the Son.
2027-01-06.resolve: Renew your baptismal promises at home this week: reject sin and profess the Creed.

intro: Theme: “Follow me.”
After his Baptism Jesus begins his ministry in Galilee. Light dawns on a land in darkness, and ordinary fishermen hear a call that changes their lives. The same call reaches us.

sub: Jesus begins not in Jerusalem but in “Galilee of the Gentiles”, a mixed and despised region.
Isaiah's promise is fulfilled: a light for the nations.
Christ still begins where people sit in darkness: in our struggles and our neighbourhoods.
q: I will give you as a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth.
The people who sat in darkness have seen a great light, and for those who sat in the region and shadow of death light has dawned.
points.apply: Pray for one person you know who is in darkness: illness, addiction, despair.

sub: God called Moses by name from the bush, and he answered: “Here I am.”
Jesus calls fishermen at their work: “Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.”
They leave their nets “immediately”: a call delayed is often a call lost.
q: God called to him out of the bush, “Moses, Moses!” And he said, “Here I am.”
And he said to them, “Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.” Immediately they left their nets and followed him.
points.apply: Ask: what “net” holds me back from following Jesus more closely? Leave it this week.

points.h: A community born of the call
sub: Those who answered became the first Church: teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread and prayer.
God heals the brokenhearted and gathers his people.
Every call to follow Christ is also a call into his Church.
q: He heals the brokenhearted, and binds up their wounds.
They devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers.
points.apply: Join one parish activity (prayer group, catechism, charity) this month. Pray for vocations.

concl: The Light has come, the call has been given, and the community is gathered.
Let us answer like Moses, “Here I am”, and like the apostles, leave our nets to follow him.
2027-01-10.resolve: Pray daily this week for priestly and religious vocations from your parish.

intro: Theme: “Come and see.”
Philip finds Nathanael and tells him about Jesus. Nathanael doubts: “Can anything good come out of Nazareth?” Philip does not argue; he invites: “Come and see.” Faith grows through encounter.

sub: Nathanael's question is honest; God is not afraid of our questions.
Wisdom promises that those who seek diligently will find.
The best answer to doubt is an invitation to meet Christ in Scripture, in the Qurbono and in a living community.
q: I love those who love me, and those who seek me diligently find me.
Nathanael said to him, “Can anything good come out of Nazareth?” Philip said to him, “Come and see.”
points.apply: Invite one person who has drifted away to come with you to Sunday Qurbono.

sub: Jesus praises Nathanael: “an Israelite in whom there is no deceit.”
God says: “I am the LORD; I sanctify you”: holiness begins with an honest heart.
Jesus already knew Nathanael under the fig tree; nothing is hidden from him.
q: You shall not profane my holy name, that I may be sanctified among the people of Israel: I am the LORD; I sanctify you.
When Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him, he said of him, “Here is truly an Israelite in whom there is no deceit!”
points.apply: Remove one falsehood from your life this week: a lie, a pretence, a double life.

points.h: Heaven opened: Christ is the ladder
sub: Jacob dreamed of a ladder with angels ascending and descending.
Jesus says: you will see heaven opened and angels on the Son of Man: he is the meeting place of heaven and earth.
In the Holy Qurbono heaven opens; we join the angels in praise.
q: And he dreamed that there was a ladder set up on the earth, the top of it reaching to heaven; and the angels of God were ascending and descending on it.
Very truly, I tell you, you will see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.
points.apply: At the Sanctus, remember that you are singing with the angels.

concl: Nathanael moved from doubt to confession: “Rabbi, you are the Son of God!”
Let us come and see, let our hearts be without deceit, and find in Christ the open heaven.
2027-01-17.resolve: Read John 1:35–51 slowly once this week and ask: where is Jesus inviting me to “come and see”?

intro: Theme: “Remembering the priests who served us.”
On Kohne Sunday the Church remembers her departed priests. We thank God for them, we pray for them, and we reflect on the gift of the priesthood that continues among us.

sub: On Mount Hor Moses took Aaron's vestments and put them on Eleazar: the ministry continues after death.
Every priest is taken from among the people and appointed for the people, to offer gifts and sacrifices.
The priests who baptised us, absolved us and fed us with the Eucharist have handed on Christ's priesthood to the next generation.
q: Moses stripped Aaron of his vestments, and put them on his son Eleazar; and Aaron died there on the top of the mountain.
Every high priest chosen from among mortals is put in charge of things pertaining to God on their behalf, to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins.
points.apply: Remember by name the priests who baptised you, gave you First Communion, married you or buried your loved ones.

points.h: Faithful stewards of the Master's gift
sub: Aaron was anointed to minister to the Lord and bless the people in his name.
In the parable of the pounds, the faithful servant is praised for trading with what he received.
Priests are judged by faithfulness, not success; so are all of us in our vocations.
q: Moses ordained him, and anointed him with holy oil; it was an everlasting covenant for him and for his descendants … to minister to the Lord and serve as priest and bless his people in his name.
He said to him, “Well done, good slave! Because you have been trustworthy in a very small thing, take charge of ten cities.”
points.apply: Encourage a priest this week with a word of thanks, and pray for one who is struggling.

sub: Judas Maccabeus offered sacrifice for the dead, “a holy and pious thought”.
The Church prays for the faithful departed, that they may be purified and enter God's rest.
Our prayers and Holy Qurbono offered for departed priests are an act of gratitude and charity.
q: But if he was looking to the splendid reward that is laid up for those who fall asleep in godliness, it was a holy and pious thought. Therefore he made atonement for the dead, so that they might be delivered from their sin.
Blessed are the dead who from now on die in the Lord. “Yes,” says the Spirit, “they will rest from their labors, for their deeds follow them.”
points.apply: Have a Holy Qurbono offered, or pray a Rosary, for a departed priest.

concl: The priests we remember today gave their lives so that Christ might be present among us.
Let us thank God for them, pray for their eternal rest, and pray that the Lord will send good and holy priests to his Church.
2027-01-24.resolve: Visit the grave of a priest in your parish cemetery and pray for him.

intro: Theme: “From death to life.”
On Aneede Sunday we remember all our departed: parents, grandparents, friends. We do not come as people without hope. We come to pray for them and to learn from them how to live.

points.h: In Christ, death is a passage to life
sub: Jacob ended his blessing, breathed his last and was “gathered to his people”.
Jesus promises: whoever hears his word and believes has already passed from death to life.
Our departed are not lost; they are on the way home, and we pray that they reach it.
q: When Jacob ended his charge to his sons, he drew up his feet into the bed, breathed his last, and was gathered to his people.
Very truly, I tell you, anyone who hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life, and does not come under judgment, but has passed from death to life.
points.apply: Name your departed loved ones in prayer each day this week.

sub: Hezekiah, facing death, turned to God and found mercy.
St Paul does not forbid grief; he forbids grief without hope.
The Church prays for the dead, that they may be purified and see God; this is an act of love (CCC 1032).
q: Surely it was for my welfare that I had great bitterness; but you have held back my life from the pit of destruction, for you have cast all my sins behind your back.

We do not want you to be uninformed … about those who have died, so that you may not grieve as others do who have no hope. For since we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so, through Jesus, God will bring with him those who have died.
points.apply: Have a Holy Qurbono offered for your departed, and visit the cemetery with your family.

points.h: We will be judged by love
sub: At the last judgment the King asks about the hungry, the stranger, the sick and the prisoner.
Proverbs says kindness to the poor is a loan to the Lord.
The best way to honour our dead is to live the works of mercy they taught us.
q: Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the LORD, and will be repaid in full.
Truly I tell you, just as you did it to one of the least of these who are members of my family, you did it to me.
points.apply: Do one work of mercy this week in memory of a departed loved one.

concl: The dead hear the voice of the Son of God; those who have done good will rise to life.
Let us pray for our departed with faith and live with charity, so that one day we may meet them in the Father's house.
2027-01-31.resolve: Pray “Eternal rest grant to them, O Lord” for the departed after each meal this week.

intro: Theme: “No one can enter the kingdom of God without being born of water and Spirit.”
New birth from above, the lifted-up Son, and gentle shepherds.

sub: Nicodemus comes by night.
Water and Spirit.
Baptism, a new birth.
q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
Jesus answered, “Very truly, I tell you, no one can enter the kingdom of God without being born of water and Spirit.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises before Denho.

sub: The bronze serpent.
Look and live.
Life flows from the Cross.
q: And the LORD said to Moses, “Make a poisonous serpent, and set it on a pole; and everyone who is bitten shall look at it and live.”
And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up,
points.apply: Spend a few minutes looking at the Cross in silence today.

sub: Mar Baselios and Mar Gregorios.
Firm in truth, kind to all.
Correcting with gentleness.
q: A soft answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
And the Lord's servant must not be quarrelsome but kindly to everyone, an apt teacher, patient, correcting opponents with gentleness.
points.apply: Pray for our Catholicos and correct others gently.

concl: Born of water and Spirit, we look to the Cross.
Like Basil and Gregory, let us be firm in faith and gentle in love.
2027-01-02.resolve: Pray each day this week for our Catholicos and bishops.

intro: Theme: “Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.”
Faith that pleases God, the Beatitudes, and the rising Sun.

sub: Abel's offering.
Enoch walked with God.
Noah built before the rain.
q: Enoch walked with God; then he was no more, because God took him.
And without faith it is impossible to please God, for whoever would approach him must believe that he exists and that he rewards those who seek him.
points.apply: Act today on one word of God you have been postponing.

points.h: Blessed are the pure in heart
sub: The Beatitudes as a portrait.
Purity of heart sees God.
St Chavara lived them.
q: Who shall ascend the hill of the LORD? And who shall stand in his holy place? Those who have clean hands and pure hearts, who do not lift up their souls to what is false, and do not swear deceitfully.
Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.
points.apply: Go to confession before Denho.

sub: Malachi, last of the prophets.
Healing in its wings.
The Sun rises at the Jordan.
q: But for you who revere my name the sun of righteousness shall rise, with healing in its wings. You shall go out leaping like calves from the stall.
You are the light of the world. A city built on a hill cannot be hid.
points.apply: Light a lamp at home for Denho.

concl: Faith, purity of heart and light belong together.
The Sun of righteousness is about to rise at the Jordan.
2027-01-04.resolve: Live one Beatitude deliberately this week.

intro: Theme: “Consider the lilies.”
Gifts for the body, growth into Christ, freedom from worry.

sub: Apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors, teachers.
To equip the saints.
Every gift is for others.
q: The spirit of the LORD shall rest on him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and the fear of the LORD.
The gifts he gave were that some would be apostles, some prophets, some evangelists, some pastors and teachers, to equip the saints for the work of ministry, for building up the body of Christ,
points.apply: Offer one gift to serve your parish this month.

sub: No longer children tossed about.
Truth in love.
The body grows in love.
q: The righteous flourish like the palm tree, and grow like a cedar in Lebanon.
But speaking the truth in love, we must grow up in every way into him who is the head, into Christ,
points.apply: Speak one needed truth this week, gently.

sub: Ravens and lilies.
You of little faith.
The Father knows.
q: Cast your burden on the LORD, and he will sustain you; he will never permit the righteous to be moved.
He said to his disciples, “Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.
points.apply: Entrust one worry to God tonight.

concl: The Father who clothes the lilies speaks tomorrow at the Jordan.
Come to Denho free of worry, ready to grow.
2027-01-05.resolve: Pray tonight for families in the diaspora.

intro: Theme: “Among those born of women no one is greater than John.”
The praise of the Baptist and the grace of the Kingdom.

sub: Firm against Herod.
Simple in the desert.
Faithful to the end.
q: The Lord GOD helps me; therefore I have not been disgraced; therefore I have set my face like flint, and I know that I shall not be put to shame;
When John's messengers had gone, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to look at? A reed shaken by the wind?
points.apply: Refuse one compromise with the truth today.

sub: The promised messenger.
The new Elijah.
He prepared the way.
q: Lo, I will send you the prophet Elijah before the great and terrible day of the LORD comes.
I tell you, among those born of women no one is greater than John; yet the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.
points.apply: Thank God for someone who prepared the way of Christ for you.

sub: Grace makes the least great.
Paul, the least of the saints.
We are sent to walk the way.
q: But the LORD said to me, “Do not say, ‘I am only a boy’; for you shall go to all to whom I send you, and you shall speak whatever I command you.
Of this gospel I have become a servant according to the gift of God's grace that was given me by the working of his power.
points.apply: Share your faith with one person this week.

concl: John was great; grace makes us greater still.
Let us walk the way he prepared.
2027-01-07.resolve: Thank God each night this week for your Baptism.

intro: Theme: “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.”
Stephen sees heaven open, forgives, and shows that service and witness are one road.

sub: Filled with the Spirit.
He sees Jesus standing.
The Jordan's open heaven again.
q: As I watched in the night visions, I saw one like a human being coming with the clouds of heaven. And he came to the Ancient One and was presented before him.
But filled with the Holy Spirit, he gazed into heaven and saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.
points.apply: Look to heaven in prayer in your next trial.

sub: Receive my spirit.
Do not hold this sin.
Saul is watching.
q: Into your hand I commit my spirit; you have redeemed me, O LORD, faithful God.

While they were stoning Stephen, he prayed, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.” Then he knelt down and cried out in a loud voice, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” When he had said this, he died.
points.apply: Pray by name for someone who has hurt you.

sub: Stephen the deacon.
The household of Stephanas.
Service and witness, one road.
q: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And I said, “Here am I; send me!”
Now, brothers and sisters, you know that members of the household of Stephanas were the first converts in Achaia, and they have devoted themselves to the service of the saints;
points.apply: Offer one service to the parish this week.

concl: The first martyr shows the whole Christian life: faith, forgiveness, service.
His prayer converted Saul; ours can change hearts too.
2027-01-08.resolve: Forgive one person from the heart this week.

intro: Theme: “Let God be proved true.”
God's faithfulness, God's commandment, and the washing of the heart.

sub: Israel's unfaithfulness.
God remains true.
His mercies are new each morning.
q: The steadfast love of the LORD never ceases, his mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.
What if some were unfaithful? Will their faithlessness nullify the faithfulness of God?
points.apply: Thank God for one sign of his faithfulness.

sub: Washing of hands.
Lips and heart.
Customs must serve God's word.
q: The Lord said: Because these people draw near with their mouths and honor me with their lips, while their hearts are far from me, and their worship of me is a human commandment learned by rote;
You abandon the commandment of God and hold to human tradition.
points.apply: Renew one devotion so that it comes from the heart.

sub: Denho and our Baptism.
Clean within.
Approach with a true heart.
q: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and put a new and right spirit within me.
let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, with our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.
points.apply: Pray Psalm 51 slowly tonight.

concl: God is faithful even when we are not.
Let our traditions be the clothing of a loving heart.
2027-01-09.resolve: Go to Qurbono tomorrow with a renewed heart.
